requirement: Create a POST /orders endpoint returning 202 Accepted, scheduling BackgroundTasks.add_task(process_order, order_id), updating in-memory ORDERS_DB status from pending to processed, recording audit log, and validating quantity > 0 with lowercase email normalization.
skeleton: FastAPI route with BackgroundTasks parameter, in-memory state transition, and audit logging.
caption: A FastAPI order intake service that accepts work with 202 and finishes it in a background task. OrderRequest is a pydantic model with order_id of at least one character, customer_email of at least three characters, item of at least one character, and quantity constrained with gt=0, so a quantity of one is accepted and zero is rejected with 422. Two module-level stores hold state: ORDERS_DB maps order ids to order dicts and AUDIT_LOG is a list of event dicts; reset_db empties both. process_order looks up the order by id, and when it exists sets its status to processed and appends an order_processed event carrying order_id, customer_email, item, and quantity to AUDIT_LOG, for every customer without regard to the email domain. POST /orders declares status 202 and takes a BackgroundTasks parameter: it raises HTTPException 409 when the order id already exists, normalizes the email by stripping whitespace and lowercasing, stores the order with status pending, schedules the work with background_tasks.add_task(process_order, order_id) passing the real callable and the id, and returns an accepted status with the order id and the pending order status. Because the task runs after the response is sent, a subsequent GET /orders/{order_id} observes status processed, and that route raises HTTPException 404 for an unknown id. GET /audit-logs returns a copy of the audit list under a logs key.

plan.intent: Accept an order immediately and process it in the background
constraints: POST /orders answers 202 with the order pending
A duplicate order id raises HTTPException 409
Quantity must be above zero and the email is stored trimmed and lowercased
The background task marks the order processed and appends an audit event
GET /orders/{order_id} raises HTTPException 404 for an unknown id

rationale.teaches: An accept-then-process endpoint: 202 status, add_task with a real callable, a state transition the worker performs, unconditional audit logging, and a quantity constraint that allows one.
rationale.why: Background work is invisible in the response, so a generated route can return 202 while nothing ever runs. The fixture inspects the in-memory state after the request, which is the only way to prove the task was scheduled and completed.

ops.docstring: Accept orders at once and finish processing them in a background task.

ops.stmt: from fastapi import BackgroundTasks, FastAPI, HTTPException, status

params.name: OrderRequest
params.doc: Payload accepted when submitting an order.

ops.source:
def reset_db() -> None:
    """Forget every order and audit entry."""
    ORDERS_DB.clear()
    AUDIT_LOG.clear()

@app.get("/orders/{order_id}")
async def get_order(order_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return one order by id, or 404 when it does not exist."""
    order = ORDERS_DB.get(order_id)
    if order is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Order not found")
    return order

candidates.why_wrong: The endpoint answers 200 instead of 202, so the client assumes the order was processed synchronously.
add_task receives None instead of process_order, so the background task crashes and the order stays pending.
The worker never sets status to processed, so every order stays pending forever.
Only partner.com customers are audit-logged, so every other order is processed without a trace.
quantity must exceed 1, so a single-item order is rejected with 422.
